The antecedent 'program' is the thing being triggered (passive relation), so the past participle is correct. Distractor pull toward 'triggering' fails because the program does not trigger something here; it gets triggered. The long-distance check (relative-clause subject = program, main verb 'directs' agrees) confirms the parse.

perOption.reason: 'the specific ways which they activate our systems' — inside the relative clause, 'they activate our systems' is already a complete S+V+O clause, leaving 'which' with no grammatical role. It must be 'in which' (adverbial), 'that' (quasi-adverbial after way(s)), or a zero relative ('the ways they activate...'). Rescue readings were actively tested: 'activate' cannot take 'ways' as an object gap since 'our systems' fills the object slot; no dislocation or reduced-clause analysis makes bare 'which' grammatical. Clearly ungrammatical.

The consequent 'would not have evolved' is past-referring, so past perfect in the if-clause is exactly right; a mixed-conditional objection does not apply. 'helped us adapt' also correctly repeats the help + bare-infinitive pattern.
